chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Friday prayer is obligatory for one who, if he prays the morning prayer in his home, will catch the Friday prayer. And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would only pray the afternoon prayer during the time of the noon prayer on all other days, so that when they had completed the prayer with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), they would return to their homes before nightfall. And that is a Sunnah until the Day of Resurrection.'

Thus, it does not contradict the first report, because this report is understood as recommending (mustahabb), since the obligation (fard) applies to one who is within a distance of two farsakhs. If one exceeds that distance, it becomes recommended for him to attend. And that which clarifies this is what the narrator of this hadith, namely Zurarah, narrated.
ai.seo_question: Is Friday prayer obligatory for everyone or only for those living nearby?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies the geographical scope of the obligatory Friday prayer, distinguishing it from the recommended prayer for those residing beyond two farsakhs. It links this ruling to the Prophet’s practical wisdom in adjusting prayer times to facilitate the community's return home before nightfall, establishing a enduring Sunnah. The text further resolves apparent contradictions by attributing the flexibility to the principle of recommendation for distant residents, as elaborated by the narrator Zurarah.
